title: A Repulsion Between the Disbelievers
summary: Page-three editorial framed around the Qur'anic doctrine of tadafu' (the divine repelling of evil by other evils) and applied to the contemporary US-Israeli confrontation with Iran. Opens by celebrating the destruction of 'the guide of the disbelievers and his exemplar', using the standard Arabic designation for the Iranian Supreme Leader, framed as delivered by the same US and Israeli air power that previously shielded Iranian forces in Mosul and Aleppo. Constructs a historical argument that the Iraqi jihad uniquely undertook the takfir of the Rafida as a religious rather than political matter, at a time when many Sunnis treated Twelver Shi'ism as merely another madhhab. Argues the destruction of Iran is more beneficial to the Ummah than further destruction of the Jews because the Ummah is more vulnerable to Shia infiltration than to overt Zionist threat. Warns against two opposing currents now visible: Sunnis tilting toward Iran in solidarity against Israel and the United States, and Sunnis tilting toward the US-Israeli axis to assist in dismantling Iran. Both rejected as jahili alignments. Predicts that Iranian missile strikes on Gulf states will accelerate public-level Gulf-Israel normalisation, while an opposing populist current of Iran sympathy will deepen. Calls for distinction (tamyiz) from both camps and warning against any 'convergence of interests' logic.
keyClaims: The Iranian Supreme Leader and senior figures around him have been killed in US and Israeli strikes.
Divine tadafu' has used US-Israeli air power to destroy the same Iranian forces it once shielded in Mosul and Aleppo.
The Iraqi jihad uniquely undertook the takfir of the Rafida as a religious rather than political matter, demolishing the idol of Shia legitimacy.
The destruction of Iran is more beneficial to the Ummah than further destruction of the Jews because Shia infiltration is a more insidious threat than overt Zionist threat.
Iranian missile strikes on Gulf states will accelerate public-level Gulf-Israel normalisation while triggering an opposing populist current of Iran sympathy.
Muslims must remain distinct from both the US-Israeli and Iranian camps and reject 'convergence of interests' rationales.
significanceAssessment: The most consequential piece in the five-issue set. The framing strongly implies the death of the Iranian Supreme Leader in a recent US-Israeli campaign, which, if accurate, marks a major regional inflection point and requires verification against open-source reporting. The strategic prediction about parallel Gulf-Israel normalisation and counter-bias Iran sympathy is sophisticated political analysis. Sets the doctrinal frame for subsequent issues' attacks on al-Qaeda and other jihadist actors that drifted toward the Iranian axis. The triptych imagery of Khamenei, Trump, and Netanyahu collapses the conflict into a single jahili field in which all three are equivalent enemies.
notes: Gregorian date converted from Hijri 16 Ramadan 1447. Page 3 editorial only. Claim of Iranian Supreme Leader's death is the editorial's framing; should be cross-checked against verified reporting in the tracker workflow.
